mmaths-2022-team-01.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-01.body:
$P_1P_2$ has length $13$ and $Q_1Q_2$ has length $8$, and they are perpendicular. They are the diagonals of the quadrilateral $P_1Q_1P_2Q_2$, so its area is $\frac12\cdot13\cdot8=52$ (half the area of the rectangle).

**Answer: 52**

mmaths-2022-team-02.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-02.body:
If the center is $0$, it lies in all four $2\times2$ subgrids, so every other cell is $2$: $1$ way. If the center is $2$, each $2\times2$ subgrid needs exactly one $0$ among its corner cell and its two edge cells. An edge cell of the big grid lies in two subgrids, a corner cell in one. The valid zero sets are: all four corners; top and bottom edge cells; left and right edge cells; and one edge cell together with the two corners of the opposite side (four ways: e.g. top edge with bottom-left and bottom-right corners). That is $1+1+1+4=7$. Total $1+7=8$.

**Answer: 8**

mmaths-2022-team-03.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-03.body:
Let $b$ own both, $c$ cat only, $d$ dog only, $n$ neither. Then $b=0.2(b+c)\Rightarrow c=4b$; $d=0.7(b+d)\Rightarrow d=\frac73b$; $n=0.5(d+n)\Rightarrow n=d=\frac73b$. The total is $b+4b+\frac73b+\frac73b=\frac{29}3b=522$, so $b=54$ and $n=\frac73\cdot54=126$.

**Answer: 126**

mmaths-2022-team-04.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-04.body:
$\underline{ABC}_b=Ab^2+Bb+C$. For even $b$ this has the parity of $C$, so $C$ must be even ($5$ choices). For odd $b$ it has the parity of $A+B+C$, so $A+B$ must be even. Pairs $(A,B)$ with $A\in\{1,\dots,9\}$, $B\in\{0,\dots,9\}$ of equal parity: odd $A$ ($5$) with odd $B$ ($5$) gives $25$; even $A$ ($4$) with even $B$ ($5$) gives $20$. Total $45\cdot5=225$.

**Answer: 225**

mmaths-2022-team-05.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-05.body:
Let $BD=CE=t$ with $0<t<3$. Then $F$ is at distance $2t$ from $B$ along $BA$ and has height $t\sqrt3$, so $[BFD]=\frac12\cdot t\cdot t\sqrt3=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}t^2$. $G$ is the midpoint of $AF$, so its height is $\frac{6\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+t\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{\sqrt3(3+t)}{2}$, and $DE=6-2t$, so $[DGE]=\frac12(6-2t)\frac{\sqrt3(3+t)}{2}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}(9-t^2)$. The sum is $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}t^2+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}(9-t^2)=\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}$, independent of $t$. So $a+b+c=9+3+2=14$.

**Answer: 14**

mmaths-2022-team-06.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-06.body:
The vowels $A,E$ are not in position $1$ and are non-adjacent, so their positions are $(2,4)$, $(2,5)$ or $(3,5)$ (in either order). For $(2,4)$ the consonants $B,C,D$ occupy positions $1,3,5$, so no two consonants are adjacent: not allowed. So the vowel positions are $\{2,5\}$ or $\{3,5\}$. "Exactly five pairs in alphabetical order" means exactly $5$ of the $10$ pairs of letters appear in increasing order (equivalently exactly $5$ inversions). Checking the remaining arrangements ($2\cdot3!+2\cdot3!=24$ of them), exactly two have $5$ increasing pairs: $BCEDA$ and $DCABE$.

**Answer: 2**

mmaths-2022-team-07.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-07.body:
Since $\angle B=90^\circ$, $AC=34$ is a diameter and the circumradius is $17$. $BXPY$ has right angles at $B$, $X$, $Y$, so it is a rectangle and $XY=BP$. $P$ is the midpoint of the semicircle on the other side of $AC$ from $B$, so $P$ is at distance $17$ from line $AC$. The distance from $B$ to $AC$ is $h=\frac{16\cdot30}{34}=\frac{240}{17}$, and $B$ is at distance $17$ from the center $O$ (midpoint of $AC$), so its foot is at distance $\sqrt{17^2-h^2}$ from $O$ along $AC$. Therefore $BP^2=(17+h)^2+(17^2-h^2)=2\cdot289+34h=578+480=1058$.

**Answer: 1058**

mmaths-2022-team-08.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-08.body:
Name the five bolded regions by their digits: $p$ for the region containing the whole first column (rows 6 to 8) and the cell in row 7, column 2; $q$ for the three top cells of columns 2 to 4; $r$ for the region containing the row 7 cells of columns 3 to 5 and the row 8, column 4 cell; $s$ for the region containing the row 8 cells of columns 2 and 3 and the row 9, column 2 cell; $t$ for the remaining region (row 8, column 5 and row 9, columns 3 to 5). The digits are distinct.

Then: 1-Down is $ppp$; 2-Down is $qpss$; 3-Down is $qrst$ (digits of column 3 from top); 5-Down is $rtt$; 9-Across is $s\,ttt$.

- 9-Across $=1000s+111t$ is divisible by $19$: the possible $(s,t)$ are $(1,4),(2,8),(5,1),(6,5),(7,9)$.
- 2-Down: $qpss+1$ divisible by $13$; 3-Down needs $q+r+s+t\ge25$, which forces large digits.
- 5-Down: $|rtt-ppp|$ divisible by $9$ means $r+2t\equiv3p\pmod9$.

Testing the five $(s,t)$ pairs against these conditions (and distinctness, nonzero leading digits) leaves only $(s,t)=(7,9)$, $p=2$, $q=5$, $r=6$. Check: $9$-Across $=7999=19\cdot421$; $2$-Down $=5277$, and $5278=13\cdot406$; $3$-Down $=5679$ has digit sum $27$; $5$-Down $=699$ and $|699-222|=477=9\cdot53$. A complete computer search over all digit assignments finds this is the unique solution.

**Solution grid:** row 6: $2\,5\,5\,5$; row 7: $2\,2\,6\,6\,6$; row 8: $2\,7\,7\,6\,9$; row 9: $\_\,7\,9\,9\,9$.

mmaths-2022-team-09.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-09.body:
Let $f(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+c$. The roots have sum $-a=1$, so $a=-1$, and $f(1)=1+a+b+c=5$ gives $b+c=5$. By Vieta $e_1=1$, $e_2=b$, $e_3=-c$, and $r_1^3+r_2^3+r_3^3=e_1^3-3e_1e_2+3e_3=1-3b-3c=1-15=-14$. The absolute value is $14$.

**Answer: 14**

mmaths-2022-team-10.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-10.body:
Coordinates (as complex numbers): $A_1=-8$, $A_2=8$, $A_3=6i$. Then $A_4=-\frac73i$ (circumcenter), and $A_5=\frac{25}8+\frac{11}6i$ (circumcenter of $A_2A_3A_4$).

Let $S$ be the spiral similarity with $S(A_1)=A_3$ and $S(A_2)=A_4$: $S(z)=\alpha z+\beta$ with $\alpha=\frac{A_4-A_3}{A_2-A_1}=-\frac{25i}{48}$ and $\beta=\frac{11i}6$. One checks $S(A_3)=A_5$. Since similarities preserve circumcenters and $A_{k+3}$ is the circumcenter of $A_kA_{k+1}A_{k+2}$, induction gives $S(A_k)=A_{k+2}$ for all $k$. The triangles $A_kA_{k+1}A_{k+2}$ therefore shrink toward the fixed point of $S$: $Z=\frac\beta{1-\alpha}=\frac{88i}{48+25i}=\frac{88(25+48i)}{2929}$, i.e. $Z=\left(\frac{2200}{2929},\frac{4224}{2929}\right)$.

Then $ZA_1^2=\frac{230400}{2929}$, $ZA_2^2=\frac{160000}{2929}$, $ZA_3^2=\frac{62500}{2929}$, $ZA_4^2=\frac{390625}{26361}$, and the total is $\frac{1525}{9}$. So $a+b=1525+9=1534$.

**Answer: 1534**

mmaths-2022-team-11.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-11.body:
Josh's target pattern has no overlap with itself (no proper prefix equals a suffix), so the expected waiting time is $3^3=27$. Ron's pattern is three of the same emoji: the expected time to get $k$ in a row is $3+3^2+\dots+3^k$, so for $k=3$: $3+9+27=39$ (from $E_k=3E_{k-1}+3$ with $E_0=0$: $E_1=3$, $E_2=12$, $E_3=39$). So $|M-N|=|27-39|=12$.

**Answer: 12**

mmaths-2022-team-12.title: Solution
mmaths-2022-team-12.body:
The triangle is right-angled at $A$ with inradius $1$. Put $A=(0,0)$, $B=(3,0)$, $C=(0,4)$, $I=(1,1)$. $AI$ is the line $y=x$, so $DE$ is the line $x+y=2$: $D=(2,0)$, $E=(0,2)$.

$P=(x,y)$ on $BC$ ($4x+3y=12$) with $PI=PB$: the perpendicular bisector of $BI$ meets $BC$ at $P=\left(\frac94,1\right)$ (check: $PB=\frac54=PI$). Similarly $Q=\left(1,\frac83\right)$ (check: $QC=\frac53=QI$).

Line $DP$: through $(2,0)$ and $\left(\frac94,1\right)$, slope $4$: $y=4x-8$. Line $EQ$: through $(0,2)$ and $\left(1,\frac83\right)$, slope $\frac23$: $y=\frac23x+2$. Intersection: $4x-8=\frac23x+2$, $x=3$, $y=4$, so $S=(3,4)$ (the fourth vertex of rectangle $ABSC$). Then $SI^2=(3-1)^2+(4-1)^2=13$.

**Answer: 13**
